title: Germany – Contractor's all-risk insurance services – Projektversicherung für DSD Starterpaket Scan -Med - Augsburg
description: Das gegenständliche Bauprojekt der DBInfraGO AG gehört zum DSD-Starterpaket „Durchfahrbarkeit des Skandinavien–Mittelmeer Korridors“ (ScanMed). Dieser Korridor bildet eines der drei Projekte des Starterpakets, er ist wiederum in mehrere Großprojekte je Netz unterteilt. Im gegenständlichen Projekt der DB InfraGo AG soll die Strecke 5300 mit DSTW-Technik sowie ETCS L2 ausgerüstet werden. Das Projekt ist aufgeteilt auf mehrere Abschnitte, es handelt sich hier um die Abschnitte PA 1 und PA 4 im Netzbezirk Donauwörth und im Netzbezirk Augsburg. Die Investitionssumme für dieses Projekt wird mit ca. EUR 271,8 Mio. veranschlagt. Hiervon sind bereits ca. EUR 10,0 Mio. über einen bestehenden Vertrag abgerechnet worden. Der hier neu ausgeschriebene Versicherungsvertrag wird den bestehenden Vertrag ablösen. Es wird mit einer derzeit geplanten Bauzeit bis zum 31.12.2030 gerechnet. Der Versicherungsvertrag beginnt nach Beendigung des Ausschreibungsverfahrens mit dem Datum des Zuschlages im Anschluss an eine derzeit bestehende Vorlaufdeckung. (Typ M) In der Haftpflichtversicherung beträgt die Deckungssumme je Schadenfall EUR 25.000.000 pauschal für Personen-, Sach- und Vermögensschäden, einschließlich der Leistungen aus der Umwelthaftpflichtversicherung. In der Planungshaftpflichtversicherung steht eine separate Deckungssumme je Schadenfall von EUR 10.000.000 pauschal für Sach- und Vermögensschäden zur Verfügung. Die vorgenannten Summen sind dreifach maximiert. Die Extended Maintenance im Teil Bauleistungs- und Montageversicherung beträgt 42 Monate. Die Nachhaftung beträgt in der Haftpflichtversicherung 10 Jahre, in der Umwelthaftpflicht- und Umweltschadenversicherung 5 Jahre. Der generelle Selbstbehalt beträgt mindestens EUR 25.000. Für Personenschäden entfällt der Selbstbehalt. In der Planungshaftpflichtversicherung ist die erweiterte Planungsdeckung eingeschlossen. Im Rahmen der erweiterten Planungsdeckung beträgt der Selbstbehalt EUR 100.000

title: Ireland – Repair and maintenance services of mechanical building installations – Fabrication and maintenance 2026
description: Dublin Bus is looking to establish a fabrication and maintenance framework with appropriate Contractors to carry out repair and maintenance at each of its facilities which consists of All locations throughout Dublin City and County. Dublin Bus wishes to establish a contract, which will provide ongoing basic fabrication and maintenance, repair and small new-works at all Dublin Bus locations There will be 2 lots under this tender. Lot 1 will account for most of the work; mechanical maintenance (fabrication) works of all facilities and small new installations (less than €15,000 ex VAT). This will be a direct-award contract to the successful contractor. Lot 1 contract value is estimated to be ca. €280k per annum excluding VAT. Lot 2 will be for larger new installation (greater than €15,000 ex VAT) additional works beyond the scope of Lot 1. It is intended to form a framework and run mini competitions for works in this category. No previous call-offs were made under this Lot however; it is included in the new framework to accommodate future requirements falling within this scope. title: NU2251 High Resolution Maskless Lithography
description: The scope of this tender covers the supply, delivery, installation and ongoing maintenance of a high resolution maskless aligner for UV (375 nm) photolithography within the new Great Northeast Nanofab (GNN) facility. The GNN is a new micro/nanofabrication clean room, hosted at Newcastle University. The intention is for the GNN to act as a regional open-access clean room for academia and low TRL commercial developments, allowing other universities and sites to specialise in a hub-and-spoke model. High-resolution photolithography has been identified as a critical capability gap at the GNN. This procurement is externally funded by the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC).

title: Activity & Interpretation Plan Consultant
description: The appointed consultant will prepare a comprehensive Activity & Interpretation Plan which demonstrates how people will engage with St Peter's Church and the wider heritage of Thetford through: • Learning; • Volunteering; • Skills development; • Community engagement; • Interpretation; • Participation; • Events; • Training; • Outreach activities. The consultant shall ensure that the Activity & Interpretation Plan is fully aligned with NLHF requirements and capable of supporting a successful Delivery Phase application. The Activity Plan shall identify opportunities for community involvement, volunteering, learning, training, events and wider public engagement, together with recommendations for sustainable delivery and long-term legacy. The Interpretation Plan shall identify and communicate the key heritage themes, stories and significance of St Peter's Church, establish target audiences, and develop recommendations for accessible and engaging interpretation that supports the project's vision and outcomes. This specification covers providing Homes for Children and Young People in Our Care, Independent Fostering Arrangements and Children's Homes. The primary role of Independent Fostering Arrangements and Children's Homes is to provide homes to ensure children in our care have a place that is safe and suitable for their individual needs, where they are supported by people who care for them and about them to achieve their full potential, develop resilience, enjoy good health and wellbeing and develop into adulthood. title: Madservice - Nordfyns Kommune
description: Nordfyns Kommune ønsker at udbyde madservice inkl. udbringning/levering til hjemmeboende borgere. Udbuddet omfatter ikke levering af mad til borgere, der bor på Kommunens plejecentre. Madservice er en ydelse tildelt efter § 13 i Ældreloven (LBK nr .1651 af 30/12/2024) og/eller Servicelovens §83 (LBK nr 1287 af 28/08/2020). Borgere i eget hjem tildeles ydelsen i henhold til Ældrelovens bestemmelser i § 18 om frit valg samt. Servicelovens § 91. Loven har til formål at sikre, at borgere i eget hjem, der er visiteret til madservice, har frit leverandørvalg. Opgaven omfatter madservice med udbringning, dvs. produktion og levering af mad. Omfanget er opgjort på baggrund af perioden juni 2025 – maj 2026 (begge inkl). Da borgerne har frit valg mellem leverandører, er omfanget af ydelser efter Aftalen, dels afhængigt af, hvor mange borgere der er berettiget til en visitation til madservice, og dels af borgernes konkrete valg af leverandør. title: User Testing Software Platform for User Experience Testing
description: Notice of Proposed Procurement (NPP) for User Testing Software Platform for User Experience Testing This bid solicitation 1000505276/B cancels and supersedes previous bid solicitation number 1000505276/A dated November 03, 2025 with a closing of December 03, 2025 at 02:00 PM EDT. The solicitation is being reissued as the previous solicitations resulted in non compliant bids. Unless otherwise stated herein, all terms and conditions of the original solicitation remain unchanged. The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) intends to enter into a contract with a single contractor for access to a user testing software platform to test CRA content on Canada.ca with the Canadian public, as well as certain niche audiences such as business owners, families with children, and other demographics as required. The ability to test with persons who use assistive reading and navigation technologies is not within scope for this requirement and has been solicited under a separate procurement by the CRA. The objective is to assess the ease with which users can find information and successfully complete tasks on Canada.ca and to identify any difficulties that users face in navigating CRA content so that solutions can be proposed and implemented to improve those performance measures. This requirement also includes irrevocable options to procure additional quantities of test requests to be used within the User Testing Software Platform annual entity license for the User Testing Software Platform for User Experience Testing. The period of any resulting contract will be for two (2) years with CRA retaining the irrevocable option to extend the period of the contract for up to five (5) additional one (1) year periods. A bid must comply with the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory evaluation criteria to be declared responsive. The responsive bid with the lowest bid evaluation price will be recommended for contract award. Proposal documents and supporting information must be submitted in either English or French. Conditional Set-Aside Under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business • This procurement may be conditionally set aside under the federal government Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business. • In order to be considered for the set-aside, the Bidder must certify that it qualifies as an Indigenous business as defined under PSIB and that it will comply with all requirements of PSIB. If bids from two (2) or more Indigenous businesses are compliant with the terms of the Request for Proposal, the contracting authority will limit the competition to those Indigenous businesses and will not consider bids from any non-Indigenous businesses that may have been submitted. • For more information on Indigenous business requirements of the Set-aside Program for Indigenous Business, refer to Eligibility for Indigenous procurement set aside and Procurement information for Indigenous business owners Questions must be directed in writing to the contracting authority via email: Christian.Nkezurukundo@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids must be submitted by using the Connect service provided by the Canada Post Corporation. When responding, the proposal MUST be delivered to: Canada Revenue Agency Bid Receiving Unit BRUg@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids will not be accepted if emailed directly to this email address. This email address must be used to request that CRA open a Connect conversation, as detailed in Appendix 3: Standard Instructions - Goods or Services - Competitive Requirements of the Request for Proposal. Bidders must not use their own licensing agreement for Connect to initiate a Connect conversation with CRA. The CRA reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement.

title: Wharf Replacement - St Bride's - NL
description: 1. TITLE Wharf Reconstruction – St. Bride’s, NL for Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) 2. SCOPE OF WORK The work consists of the furnishing of all plant, labour, equipment and material for wharf reconstruction at St. Bride’s, NL, in strict accordance with specifications and accompanying drawings and subject to all terms and conditions of the Contract. Work will consist of, but will not necessarily be limited to, the following: • Demolition and removal of the existing northwest breakwater wharf, as noted on the drawings. title: Weak magnetic anomaly detection for defence and security
description: *Please note that the ISC website will be available on October 30, 2026* This Challenge Notice is issued under the Innovative Solutions Canada Program (ISC) Call for Proposals 004 (EN578-24ISC4). For general ISC information, Offerors can visit the ISC website at: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en Please refer to the Solicitation Documents Innovative Solutions Canada Program Call for Proposals – 004 - Tender Notice | CanadaBuys https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 which contains the process for submitting a proposal. Steps to apply: Step 1: Read this challenge. Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/weak-magnetic-anomaly-detection-defence-and-security?auHash=1sFpxB6DzXI5S5IfIex1eysacfiS2cUIMVE1Eeit0EQ ISED is seeking a novel magnetometer (either quantum or classical or a combination thereof) that provides advantage over existing capabilities either in sensitivity, specificity, or Size, Weight, Power and Cost (SWaP-C), and multi-domain employability. Challenge sponsor: Innovation, Sciences et Développement économique Canada (ISDE) Funding mechanism: Contract Opening date: October 30, 2026 Closing date: November 27, 2026 14:00 Eastern time Challenge Problem statement Canada has a requirement for magnetic anomaly detection for defence and security. Traditional magnetometers, such as fluxgate sensors, have been used for decades to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. A fluxgate magnetometer is a relatively simple classical device: it consists of a coil of wire wrapped around a core material and detects changes in magnetic flux passing through the sensor. While reliable, these classical sensors face inherent limitations in size, sensitivity, accuracy, and long term stability. Quantum magnetometers, by contrast, leverage the principles of quantum mechanics and promise the ability to achieve superior performance. They offer enhanced sensitivity, improved accuracy and stability, and in some cases even reduced size and weight compared to their classical counterparts. There is a lack of suitably mature quantum sensors in the commercial space. The government of Canada has identified a need to develop a device or system consisting of hardware and software and a quantum sensor or a mix of classical and quantum sensors capable of sensing nanotesla (nT) or even femtotesla (fT) magnetic signals that can be used for a myriad of commercial, medical, and defence applications. In scanning the research underway, there appears to be interest in various means for the sensing of magnetic fields, including but not limited to Superconducting Quantum Interference Devices (SQUID), Superconducting Quantum Interference Filter (SQIF), and (Nitrogen Vacancy (NV) diamond. In addition to this we are led to believe that Rydberg atoms, typically framed for electric field detection can be reconfigured and/or adapted for magnetic field detection as well. We are also aware of another technology termed Spin-Exchange Relaxation-Free (SERF) which is very sensitive, but so sensitive as to be problematic to employ. This investigation seeks to explore nT and even fT sensitivities. Desired outcomes and considerations Essential (mandatory) outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Essential range and direction finding considerations Demonstrate sensing capabilities of magnetic anomalies in close proximity where distance (d) is greater than or equal to (=) 2 meters (m) with a relative error less than 10%. The device must provide azimuth to +/- 5 degrees, and an inclination of +/- 5 degrees. 2. Sensitivity Produce a prototype capable of a minimum of 500 picotesla (pT) sensitivity with a target of 10 fT. 3. Specificity The device must be able to separate a target signal from background noise. A sensitive magnetometer will detect a plethora of magnetic fields in a given cluttered environment, but the user will be interested in the absence or presence of a target signal. The device must detect and identify three specific Steel 1018 ferromagnetic targets at a minimum distance of 10 meter through free space. It must achieve a 95% true positive rate (TPR) for both detecting the presence of a target and classifying which specific target is present. 4. Rough characterization Demonstrate ability to characterize the nature of the source in rough order of magnitude – i.e. point source vs larger objects +/- 5 centimeters (cm). 5. Latency Readout less than or equal to (=) 200 milliseconds (ms) meaning sensing, ranging, azimuth, and inclination reading allowing dynamic device sensor use for object or enclosure survey. This 200 ms is the total time from sensing to displaying the result to the human user. This time includes physical sensing, processing to the point the user is provided useful data. 6. Sense through barrier capability Ability for device to sense through paramagnetic barrier materials such as walls (including but not limited to wood, gypsum board, plaster, insulation material) with some barriers inundated with clutter from other materials such as steel studs, nails, screws, pipes and other ferromagnetic materials. 7. Prototype description All parts/components fully integrated in one system of systems, including but not limited to power, API/software, hardware (sensor, cooler – if applicable). 8. Power Power consumption must be 50 W or less. Integrated replaceable power supply offering at least eight (8) hours of cordless and continued operation at temperatures ranging between 16°C and 40°C at a relative humidity between 30 and 60%. 9. Human factors Must be lightweight and compact/portable (e.g.; hand-carried, “shoulderable”, body worn). 10. Size and weight Volumetric dimensions =117,232 cm^3 (77 x 52.5 x 29 cm); maximum weight = 15Kg. 11. Environmental considerations The initial device must be designed at least for indoor use at temperatures ranging between 16°C to 30°C with relative humidity between 30-60% 12. Per unit cost Must show that a finished device can be made under $60,000 CAD. Additional Outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Desirable range It is desirable to have a device that has greater standoff range in excess of 2m. The accuracy in ranging the MA would ideally be less than 1% relative error. Maximum sensing distance is desirable. The device should provide an azimuth to +/- 1 degree, and an inclination of +/- 1 degree. 2. Rough characterization The device provides a rough but human interpretable shape of the object, that allows the object to be characterized or even identified. 3. Sensitivity Produce a prototype capable of surpassing 10 fT sensitivity. 4. Specificity Ability to characterize and identify magnetic anomalies (objects with a known magnetic signature). 5. Quiet Device should be silent (vibration/audible signature). 6. Desired Configuration Device does not emit acoustic, electromagnetic (EM), and/or heat signature. Can run in both low and high humidity in temperature extremes from -20 to +40C, under conditions of vibration, and through cluttered barriers (e.g.; barrier material convoluted with wiring, and magnetic structural material) 7. Target Scale Desirable to be used against both large (room sized) and small (hardware or package sized) enclosures or objects. 8. Static vs oscillating field detection Ability to differentiate between static and oscillating magnetic fields. 9. Characterization of magnetic anomalies/sources Ability to characterize and identify magnetic anomalies. Ability to discern shape and size +/- 1 cm. 10. Human factor / accessibility considerations Device should be suitably adapted as to be easy to train on, easy to use (intuitive), and be in a shape or form factor that is amenable for the operator to use in both open and confined settings. The device should be man portable. Hum

title: GUARD SERVICES NATIONAL CAPITAL REGION (NRC)
description: This bid solicitation is being issued to satisfy the requirement of Shared Services Canada (SSC). It is intended to result in the award of 1 contract for 2 years plus 5 one-year irrevocable options allowing Canada to extend the term of the contract(s). Service Description Shared Services Canada (SSC) requires the provision of professional security guard services at various facilities located throughout the National Capital Region (NCR), including Ottawa, Ontario and Gatineau, Quebec. The Contractor shall provide qualified security personnel to ensure the protection of SSC employees, visitors, information, facilities, and assets. title: CMMA Composite Repair Shelter
description: The Department of National Defence (DND), through the Canadian Multi-Mission Aircraft (CMMA) Project, requires the design, manufacture, and delivery of a clean room facility to serve as an interim Composite Repair Shelter at 14 Air Maintenance Squadron (14 AMS), 14 Wing Greenwood, Nova Scotia. The shelter will be installed within Hangar 10, which has existing temperature-control capabilities, and will remain in service until the construction of the new CMMA hangar. The Composite Repair Shelter will support aircraft composite repair activities, including the application and curing of adhesives, bonds, lacquers, and resins used on composite materials such as carbon fibre, fiberglass, and aramid fibre. Limited quantities of solvents, including acetone, methyl isobutyl ketone (MIBK), and methyl propyl ketone (MPK), will be used during repair operations.

title: Microsoft Power Apps and Power Automate Development and Support Services
description:
The Canton of St. Gallen is introducing the Microsoft Power Platform as part of its digital workplace under the DRIVE program. The technical platform, operating model, and the fundamental governance, architecture, and security requirements are provided by the Canton of St. Gallen and its existing service providers. The Microsoft Power Platform will be made available to the canton's organizational units as a standardized platform for the digitization and automation of business processes.

In particular, Microsoft Power Apps and Microsoft Power Automate will be used to develop and enhance applications, digital forms, approval and workflow solutions, as well as other process automation initiatives. Depending on the use case, the standard connectors approved within the cantonal Microsoft 365 environment may be utilized.

To ensure professional implementation, the Canton requires additional external expertise and capacity. All solutions must comply with the applicable requirements relating to architecture, governance, information security, data protection, quality assurance, documentation, and operations. They must be transparent, maintainable, and documented in a manner that enables an orderly handover, operation, support, and further development.

To provide flexible coverage for future demand, which cannot be fully determined in advance, the Canton intends to conclude separate framework agreements with three qualified providers. These framework agreements will be identical in content. Individual assignments will be awarded in accordance with the call-off procedures defined in the tender documentation and the framework agreements.

title: Forbruksartikler til renhold og kantinedrift
description: Bakgrunn og formål Vestfold fylkeskommune har i dag en rammeavtale for kjøp av renholds-, papir-, plast- og storkjøkkenprodukter. Avtalen har sluttdato i januar 2027, og det er derfor behov for å gjennomføre en ny anskaffelse for å etablere en ny rammeavtale fra samme tidspunkt. Anskaffelsen skal dekke fylkeskommunens løpende behov for varer og tilhørende tjenester til renhold og kantinedrift ved videregående skoler, tannklinikker, museer og fylkeshuset. Formålet er å sikre stabil forsyning, effektiv drift og lik kvalitet over tid på tvers av lokasjoner. Det er samtidig et mål at den nye rammeavtalen legger til rette for et hensiktsmessig standardsortiment med nødvendige lokale tilpasninger, god sortimentsstyring og en brukervennlig bestillingsløsning. Fylkeskommunen ønsker også produkter og emballasjeløsninger med bedre miljøegenskaper, samt sikker kompatibilitet mellom forbruksartikler, dispensere og maskiner. Produktgrupper det er behov for er: Avfallshåndtering Hygieneprodukter Kantineprodukter Renoldsmidler Renholdsprodukter Tørkepapir

description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) AND NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. This Sources Sought Synopsis is being used as a market research tool to determine the availability and adequacy of potential qualified small business sources prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation for architect-engineer services. All Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (VOSB), Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Businesses (EDWOSB), Women-Owned Small Businesses (WOSB), Small Disadvantaged Businesses (SDB) certified under the Small Business Administration�s (SBA�s) 8(a) Business Development Program, Historically Underutilized Business Zone Small Businesses (HUBZone SB) certified by SBA, and all other small businesses are encouraged to respond. Responses to this notice will determine the feasibility and/or basis for the Navy�s decision to proceed with an acquisition. Information received in relation to this notice will be used to assist the Government in developing an overall acquisition strategy, including the type and number of contracts and use of small business concerns. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources as a result of this synopsis. Large business submittals will not be considered. NAVFAC Atlantic is seeking to identify potential sources with the capacity, experience and interest in competing for a contract for a Single Award Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Architect-engineering (A/E) Contract for Environmental Planning and Engineering Services of an interdisciplinary nature for the implementation of National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), Executive Order (EO) 12114, Environmental Effects Abroad of Major Federal Actions �Ship Homeporting and Related Operational Issues. The principal geographic area covered by this contract encompasses NAVFAC Atlantic's AOR, NAVFAC Pacific�s AOR and the adjacent waters of the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, including the Continental United States, the Caribbean, Europe, and North Africa. Additionally, tasks associated with this contract may be assigned anywhere in the world. The NAICS code for this proposed procurement is 541330 (small business size standard is $25.5 million). If the solicitation is issued, the solicitation will consist of a base period and four (4) one-year options totaling five (5) years of performance. The anticipated total work to be issued over the life of the contract via task orders (base year plus four one-year options) shall not exceed the estimated maximum amount of $75 million. The successful contractor to any forthcoming solicitation shall provide all labor, management, supervision, tools, materials, and all equipment necessary to perform the services listed below. The preponderance of the work under this contract shall involve the accomplishment of work in the following major categories, including but not limited to: The general scope of this contract requires engineering services, biological science, physical science, cultural resource, community planning, and military operations specialists. The engineers and community planners providing services under this contract must have competence attested by a licensor as a professional engineer or certified planner. The services required from the A-E firm or joint venture include, but are not limited to, architectural-engineering (A-E) or environmental services for the preparation of environmental planning documentation such as categorical exclusions (CATEX), environmental assessments (EAs), and environmental impact statements (EISs) under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), environmental consultations and permits, as well as environmental reviews and environmental studies under EO 12114. The preponderance of the work under this contract shall be the preparation of various documents to support the proposed infrastructure-related actions with respect to ship homeporting issues. Examples of taskings required to complete this work may include analysis of port facility and infrastructure construction, renovation, and/or demolition; dredging; base realignment and closure (BRAC) actions; and proposed operational actions related to ship homeporting, waterfront activities and manned and unmanned asset activities. The contractor shall use the most up to date guidelines for preparation of the NEPA documentation. This includes Navy Instructions and the current version of the OPNAV 5090.1, Environmental Readiness Program, Marine Corps Instructions and the most current version of the P509.2, DoD Instruction 4715.11/12, and Department of War NEPA Implementing Procedures. Additionally, other tasks, studies, surveys, or documents may be required to complete the environmental planning documents including, but not limited to, environmental documentation for ship readiness and testing and training operations at the homeport locations and within Department of Defense-managed seaspace and Navy/Marine Corps training ranges, sketches, preliminary plans, cost estimates, descriptive text for future planning and work plans, modeling, geospatial analysis, information technology applications, traffics modeling and analysis, air quality modeling and analysis, noise modeling and analysis, encroachment analysis, and development and reproduction of a variety of public outreach materials of different media. For major testing and training exercises, the contractor shall be tasked with estimating marine mammal exposure from ordnance and sonar activities. In order to complete environmental planning documents in compliance with NEPA and EO 12114 and 12898, and in accordance with applicable DOD instructions, the contractor may be required to complete title: U.S. Mission Burundi Local Guard Program
description: The Department of State is conducting market research to determine the degree of interest and capability by all business sizes (small and large) in providing local guard services at the U.S. Embassy Bujumbura, Burundi. The Department of State, Bureau of Diplomatic Security plays an essential role in ensuring that foreign policy missions are accomplished in a safe and secure environment. The primary mission of the local guard service is to provide protection for United States personnel, facilities, and equipment from damage or loss due to violent attack and theft. The local guard services shall prevent unauthorized access; protect life; maintain order; deter criminal and terrorist attacks against employees, dependents, and property; and prevent damage to all U.S. assets. The NAICS code for these services is 561612. Responses must clearly demonstrate capabilities through examples of previous and/or current guard security contracts or experience closely related thereto. Vendors must specifically address the following capabilities: Current licenses, work authorizations in compliance with host country law required for the execution of work, including firearms permits and licenses. Licenses must be in the name of the U.S. business. Knowledge of and compliance with host country labor law which may require bonuses, specific minimum wage levels, premium pay for holidays, payments for social security, pensions, severance pay, sick or health benefits, childcare or any other benefit Knowledge of and compliance with host country tax law Ability to provide all types of insurance coverage required by host country in performance of services, such as automobile liability, comprehensive general liability, worker�s compensation, employer�s liability, etc. Furnishing, operating, and maintaining a radio network, including acquiring all licenses and permits that may be required for frequencies and the operation of all communications equipment Familiarity or experience with associated security equipment such as Guard Electronic Monitoring System (GEMS), Central Alarm Monitoring systems (CAMS), closed-circuit television systems, x-ray and explosive detection equipment Furnishing guard force equipment such as uniforms, vehicles, and weapons Ability to overcome language barriers Capability of instructing, providing, and qualifying personnel in the use of firearms, as well as x-ray equipment and radio equipment, including obtaining the access to a firearm training facility Ability to maintain a guard staff on a 24 hour 7 day a week basis with the ability to immediately backfill vacant positions due to resignations, rotations and illnesses due to a variety of reasons such as flu and food poisoning Capability of dealing with organized actions by direct labor personnel such as strikes (anticipated and unanticipated) and labor unrest (work slowdowns and/or organized failure of employees to report for shift changes) Ability to hire and train, including English language training and weapons training, if required, a guard staff consisting of host country nationals Ability to provide trained equipment technicians for all vehicles, radios and weapons required in the performance of the contract Ability to train a sizeable workforce to adapt quickly to unfamiliar laws and customs as well as the ability of company officials to gain quickly information regarding the laws and customs needed to maintain and equip such a workforce Experience or capability of getting contractor-furnished equipment and goods through customs and/or similar governmental agencies of the host country Understanding import and export regulations Understanding and familiarity of the Arms Export Control Act (AECA) and International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR) and the capability of complying with both by the performance date of any contract awarded requiring the execution of this Statute (22 U.S.C. 2778-2780) Managing smooth contract transition efforts. Ability to safely keep and track Government-Furnished Property Ability to screen personnel to meet suitability requirements for guard force positions Strong skill in instant, situational decision-making, e.g., response to threats Organized billing and invoicing procedures It is requested that all interested parties submit their capabilities by e-mail to Brian Averhart at AverhartB@state.gov addressing each of the above requirements by 12:00 EST, 27 November 2026. Interested parties shall also complete the attached Contractor Information Sheet. If you have any questions or comments, please reference this Sources Sought Notice when emailing. At this time, the U.S. Department of State does not guarantee that any future contracts may be awarded covering the aforementioned duties and responses to this Sources Sought notice do not bind the U.S. Department of State to any agreement with the responder, be it explicit or implied.

title: Z2DA--666-27-102 Lightning Protection Update B71N
description: GENERAL: Introduction: An inspection for current code compliance of the lightning Protection System on Building 71N has been conducted and found the system needs upgrades and repairs to meet current NFPA 780 and UL96A standards. The Sheridan VA Medical Center needs the services of a qualified contractor to perform the needed lightning protection upgrades to the main hospital building 71N. Located on the Sheridan Wyoming Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC) campus, at 1898 Fort Road, Sheridan, Wyoming 82801. Statement of Work: Specifics a. Existing Conditions The existing lightning protection system (LPS) for Building 71N was installed in 1989 during the building s original construction. Overall, the system remains in fair condition, though it requires repair because several air terminals have become detached from their adhesive bonds to the roof surface. Air terminals are present at all high points of the structure, and all roof-mounted equipment and appurtenances are properly grounded. A main grounding bus connects the communication systems and possibly the electrical distribution system to the primary service ground. The specific location where the grounding system bonds together the structural steel, electrical system, lightning protection components, and plumbing to create an equipotential ground could not be identified during the assessment. A continuous grounding loop encircles Buildings 9, 71, and 71N, with all roof air terminals and down conductors tied into this loop. Down conductors descend to the loop at the corners of each of these buildings. Each air terminal has at least two separate grounding paths, satisfying current code requirements. No Transient Voltage Surge Suppression (TVSS) devices were observed in the system. The lower 8 feet of the ground down conductors are encased in PVC electrical conduit for protection. New Construction Recent construction has added large equipment and a screen wall to the roof, which now obstructs and interferes with the original positioning of the existing air terminals. This new equipment sits higher than the existing lightning protection system components, rendering the current air terminals ineffective at intercepting and safely directing lightning strikes to ground. Project Requirements To bring the existing lightning protection system (LPS) into compliance the following corrections are needed: Install Transient Voltage Surge Suppression (TVSS) devices at the building s main service panel. Establish proper bonding by interconnecting all electrical systems, communication systems, piping, and structural steel at the service entrance to create an equipotential ground. Repair all roof air terminals that have detached or pulled away from their adhesive mounts on the roof surface. Install new air terminals at both ends of each screen wall, with additional terminals spaced at 20-foot intervals along the top of each wall, and at the highest point of the HVAC ductwork. Install an air terminal at each corner of the new HVAC equipment. Connect all newly installed air terminals to the existing LPS using #2 bare copper conductors. After these corrections have been completed, a qualified inspection is required to verify full compliance with NFPA 780 and UL 96A standards. Upon successful inspection, a Master Label Certificate should be issued for the lightning protection system. General: Construction project is to be completed within 120 calendar days from date of Notice to Proceed (NTP). Contractor shall provide all equipment, materials, supplies, tools, software, supervision, and labor required for this project, which may include, but is not limited to, demolition work, providing negative pressure environment for work, and providing all new equipment, utilities, and room finishes as indicated in the plans and this SOW per VA construction standards. Safety submittals shall be completed and approved prior to the commencement of on-site construction work. Material selection submittals shall be completed and approved prior to ordering of materials for the project. The building tenants not in the construction areas will remain at work in the buildings during this construction. Patients will remain on the floor in areas not under construction, so the contractor shall make patient safety, and infection control measures a priority. The contractor shall coordinate work locations and schedules with VA COR to minimize impact to building tenants. All electrical, carpentry, architectural, mechanical work, product design, project management, and other work needed on this project shall be provided by the Contractor. All required electrical work, low, medium, or high voltage, shall be installed and terminated by the Contractor. No wiring or cabling shall be abandoned in place. All piping, cabling, and wiring shall be labeled. All cabling and patch cabling shall match the VAMC s station-standard colors. The installation must, at a minimum, be in accordance with all applicable codes indicated in the Department of Veterans Affairs Design Manuals and VA .PUBLICATIONS (Master Construction Specifications, Construction Standards, National Fire Protection Association (NFPA), Underwriters Laboratory (UL), International Building Code IBC 2003, and National Electric Code (NEC) building codes and standards and the VA Information Security Handbook 6500.6, 6550.0 etc.). The Contractor shall read and be familiar with the most current editions of the applicable codes, standards, guides, and manuals. Sources can be accessed at the Office of Construction and Facilities Management s Technical Information Library (TIL) (http://www.cfm.va.gov/TIL). Any penetrations through any floors, ceilings, or walls shall be fire caulked, or otherwise fire sealed, and shall be done in this contract to meet VA standards and NFPA standards. Contractor shall utilize the VAMC s station-standard fire stop products or approved equal product(s). The station-standard products are SpecSeal fire caulk product is SpecSeal SSS Intumescent Firestop Sealant; and, if needed, the SpecSeal Composite Sheet may be used in areas approved by the COR. The Contractor shall inquire of the COR if any existing equipment, fixtures, hardware, doors, frames, or any other property removed is desired to be retained by the VA for reuse elsewhere within the medical center, at the time of removal. If the VA desires to retain an item, the Contractor shall deliver it to a location designated by the COR. If the VA does not desire to retain an item, the Contractor shall dispose of it properly off-station. The new components installed shall be tested and commissioned, re-certified, and/or tested before VA acceptance. All testing parameters shall be provided by the Contractor with source references to the COR and 3rd-party reviewer before testing begins. Copies of all test reports must be provided to the COR. HVAC systems that have changes made to them as part of this project, beyond diffuser replacement, shall be tested and balanced by the Contractor. Any IT data cables installed or modified as part of this effort shall be tested after installation. Test methods and plans shall be coordinated with the COR. Any Med Gas systems modified as part of this effort shall be re-certified back to the closest shut-off in the system. The Contractor shall arrange for any required re-certification as part of this contract and shall provide plans and results to the COR for approval. Fire alarm devices that are tied into the building fire alarm system, that are replaced or relocated as a result of this work, shall be tested before that phase of the project is complete. The Contractor shall arrange for all required fire alarm testing. If a building s fire alarm system is under warranty, testing must be accomplished by the contractor who holds the warranty. Any fire sprinklers that are relocated as part of this project shall be reviewed and approved by VA Safety prior to installation. All fire sprinkler work shal

title: Z2DA--523A4-CSI-288 3.0T MRI Site Prep - Design Build West Roxbury VA Medical Center (VAMC_ West Roxbury, MA
description: Page 1 of 1 INTRODUCTION: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) anticipates soliciting proposals and subsequently awarding a single Firm-Fixed-Price contract for the design-build (DB) project #523A4-CSI-288 West Roxbury VA Medical Center located in West Roxbury, MA. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-build approach. The anticipated solicitation will be issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) in accordance with FAR Parts 36 and 15, considering Technical and Price Factors. This project requires comprehensive design-build services for the the 3T MRI Site Preparation Design Build project at the West Roxbury VA Medical Center (VAMC) located in West Roxbury, MA. This project will provide construction of a temporary mobile Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) suite as well as all utility services and finishes necessary in the designated locations to allow for the installation of an MRI system by the Equipment Contractor. The work shall include, but not limited to, all labor, transportation, materials, apparatus, tools, equipment and permits necessary to provide for the renovation of the rooms, removal of the existing equipment, flooring, ceiling, sinks, casework, doors, shielding and installation of new flooring, ceiling, casework, doors, sinks, lighting, painting, med gas, shielding divider and relocation of electrical and HVAC work. Work to be performed at VAMC West Roxbury in accordance with the Statement of Work, Specifications, Drawings, Federal, State, and Local Codes. Strict noise and infection control measures shall be always followed. Off-hours and weekend work may be required to complete contractual requirements due to the location and sensitivity of the patient population. Existing life safety systems within Building 1 shall not be impaired at any time during the performance of the work. ADMINISTRATIVE: The anticipated solicitation will be issued as an RFP in accordance with FAR Part 36.3 Two Phase Design Build Selection Procedures and FAR Part 15 Contracting by Negotiation. The solicitation will be advertised as an SDVOSB set-aside. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45 million. The solicitation is anticipated to be issued in early November 2026. The period of performance is approximately 430 calendar days from the issuance of the Notice to Proceed. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $2,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. This notice is not a request for competitive offers. All questions must be submitted in writing to the issuing office via email to the CS and CO: Dawn.Schydzik@va.gov and William.Henkel@VA.gov . Telephone calls will not be accepted. -END-

title: Solicitation: Construct Combat Rescue Helicopter Flight Simulator Facility at Moffett ANGB
description: The Contractor shall provide non-personal services, to include all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a Combat Rescue Helicopter (CRH) Operational Flight Trainer (OFT) simulator facility at Moffett Air National Guard Base (ANGB), Mountain View, California. This project will provide an approximately 8,202 gross square foot building consisting of a multi-story, high bay area to house the CRH-OFT simulator, with a single-story area containing CRH mission planning, briefing and debriefing rooms, administrative areas for training and support staff, OFT maintenance and parts storage rooms, secure and non-secure telecommunication rooms, latrine facilities and mechanical, electrical and utility support rooms utilizing conventional design and construction. The building will be of permanent construction with electrical, mechanical, HVAC, plumbing, wet sprinkler fire suppression, fire detection, access control, direct digital control, and utility management. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Air space and insulation to be located inside the cavity wall to meet Energy Code requirements. The primary roofing materials will be standing seam metal roofing to match other installation facilities and the perimeter sloped roof design will include a prefinished standing seam metal roof panel system over rigid insulation. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Main entrance doors will be a pair of anodized aluminum storefront entrance doors with insulating glass including a sidelight. The Mechanical, Electrical, Sim Bay and secondary egress doors will be painted, insulated hollow metal door and frames with controlled access. Antiterrorism/Force Protection elements are incorporated. Supporting facilities include landscaping, utilities, pavements, storm drainage, sanitary sewer, site improvements, communications support, cybersecurity control systems, and tempest security.

The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. description: Το έργο αφορά την πλήρη μελέτη και κατασκευή του Αυτοκινητόδρομου Δένειας – Ακακίου - Αστρομερίτη, 4 λωρίδων κυκλοφορίας, συνολικού μήκους περίπου 18 km. Θα συνδέει τον αυτοκινητόδρομο Λευκωσίας-Κοκκινοτριμιθιάς με τον αυτοκινητόδρομο Αστρομερίτη-Ευρύχου και θα διέρχεται νότια των χωριών Ακακίου, Περιστερώνας και Αστρομερίτη. Η τυπική διατομή περιλαμβάνει 4 λωρίδες κυκλοφορίας 3,5 μ έκαστη με κεντρική νησίδα και με ασφαλτοστρωμένα ερείσματα εκατέρωθεν, πλάτους 3,0 μ. title: DLA-RFI-CT-2027-WBOS-MKTRES
description: DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY (DLA) TROOP SUPPORT CLOTHING AND TEXTILES DIRECTORATE � PHILADELPHIA, PA REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) & SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Whole-of-Government Web-Based Ordering System (WBOS) & Commercial eMarketplace Platform FEDERAL MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE (FAR 15.201(e) & FAR Part 10): This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research, planning, and information-gathering purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. The Government is seeking broad industry input on commercial capabilities, architectural options, and market readiness. Responses are strictly voluntary; the Government will not reimburse any costs associated with preparing or submitting responses to this notice. 1. Executive Summary & Purpose of Inquiry The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support Clothing and Textiles (C&T) Directorate is conducting market research to explore commercial software solutions, digital eMarketplace architectures, and industry best practices for deploying a next-generation Web-Based Ordering System (WBOS). DLA�s Troop Support C&T organization serves as the Federal Government�s primary enterprise manager for military clothing and textiles, working extensively with domestic industry. DLA is currently assessing the expansion of this shared-services procurement model to serve civilian Whole-of-Government (WOG) partner agencies, including the Department of the Interior (DOI), Department of Justice (DOJ), Department of Transportation (DOT), Department of State (DOS), and Department of Homeland Security (DHS). The primary objective of this RFI is to engage commercial e-commerce developers, SaaS providers, systems integrators, and domestic textile industry stakeholders. DLA seeks to understand what commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) capabilities exist today, how commercial technology can resolve complex federal supply chain and fiscal integration challenges, and what industry recommendations DLA should incorporate into its upcoming acquisition strategy. DLA is committed to adopting commercial best practices and avoiding custom development wherever commercial platforms can satisfy or be adapted to meet mission requirements. 2. Administrative Overview & Acquisition Milestones Market Research Parameter: Information & Acquisition Guidance Document Identifier: DLA-RFI-CT-2027-WBOS-MKTRES Anticipated Acquisition Approach: Commercial Solutions Opening (10 U.S.C. � 3458) / Commercial Acquisition (FAR Part 12 / Agile Authorities) Primary NAICS Code: 541512 - Computer Systems Design Services (Small Business Size Standard: $34.0M) Secondary NAICS Codes: 518210 - Data Processing, Hosting, and Related Services ($40.0M), 541519 - Other Computer Related Services ($34.0M) Product Service Code (PSC): DA01 - IT and Telecom - Business Application/Application Development Software RFI Issuance Date: Friday, October 30, 2026 Industry Questions & Clarifications Due: Friday, November 06, 2026, at 16:00 EST Government Formal Q&A Responses Posted: Friday, November 20, 2026 RFI Capability Response Deadline: Friday, November 27, 2026, at 16:00 EST Anticipated Pre-Solicitation Industry Day: December 2, 2026 (Virtual) Primary Contract Specialist: Courtney Hunter, Contract Specialist, DLA Troop Support C&T (Courtney.Hunter@dla.mil) Primary Contracting Officer: Ryan Zarkowski, Individual Protection and Commercial Solutions Division Chief, DLA Troop Support (Ryan.Zarkowski@dla.mil) Submission Channel: Electronic submission via email to Government POCs (Subject: 'WBOS RFI Response - [Company Name]') 3. Mission Needs & Strategic Challenges The contemplated capability would enable Government-approved vendors to list and maintain Government-approved catalogs; enable authorized agency personnel to purchase authorized items; apply agency-specific eligibility, entitlement/allowance, item-authorization, approval, and management-control rules; support authorized payment methods; and provide auditable transaction, fulfillment, and program-management information. To modernize uniform procurement across DoD and civilian partner agencies, any future solution must address several interrelated operational and regulatory challenges. Rather than dictating prescriptive technical designs, DLA outlines the desired functional outcomes below to invite innovative, industry-driven solutions: Operational Domain: The Operational Challenge / Desired Outcome Commercial Marketplace & User Experience: Deliver a modern, consumer-grade multi-tenant e-commerce experience with sub-second catalog search, faceted filtering, mobile responsiveness, and intuitive uniform selection, while supporting distinct tenant agency branding (DoD, DOI, DOJ, DOT, DOS, DHS) and role-based permissions. Domestic Provenance & Supply Chain Integrity: Because DLA operates as a central procurement hub utilizing the Defense Working Capital Fund (DWCF), end-items transacted through DLA are subject to 100% domestic sourcing requirements under the Berry Amendment (10 U.S.C. � 4862). DLA requires automated mechanisms to verify domestic origin down to the raw material/mill level, screen supply chains for forced labor or prohibited foreign entities, and prevent unverified items from being purchased. Statutory Competition & Micro-Purchases: In a multi-vendor marketplace environment, transactions must respect federal competition mandates (such as CICA and simplified acquisition thresholds). The Government seeks automated, user-friendly marketplace workflows that promote fair competition, facilitate dynamic quoting between micro-purchase thresholds ($15k) and simplified acquisition threshold ($350k), and prevent improper order splitting without creating administrative bottlenecks. Uniform Customization & Value-Added Logistics: Civilian law enforcement and military personnel require customized uniforms (e.g., branch tapes, badges, department patches, embroidery, reflective safety trims, and tailored sizing). The system must support interactive customization, dimensionally accurate digital proofing, supervisor approvals, and tracking of value-added tailoring services while ensuring all component materials remain compliant. Interagency Accounting & Fiscal Guardrails: The system must handle interagency funding across diverse partner departments without risking Antideficiency Act (ADA) violations. This includes integrating with federal financial frameworks (such as Treasury G-Invoicing Form 7600A/B), managing annual individual officer uniform allowances (5 U.S.C. � 5901), supporting multi-payment split tender (allowance + GPC + personal card overages), and reconciling DLA cost-recovery surcharges without contractor fee retention. Cybersecurity & Enterprise Interoperability: The platform will process sensitive federal uniform requisitions, military supply chain data, and law enforcement personnel information. It must meet high federal cybersecurity baselines (such as FedRAMP and DoD Cloud Computing Security Requirements), support CAC/PIV single sign-on, and interface with federal backbones such as DLA Enterprise Business System (EBS/SAP), PIEE/WAWF, and SAM.gov. Training & Performance Tracking: Provide general user training, program manager training, etc. Implement all necessary work and time management control processes to ensure timely accurate accomplishment of work requirements as well as to permit tracking work in progress. 4. Areas of Inquiry & Market Research Questionnaire Industry respondents are invited to address the following questions. Offerors may respond to all or selected inquiry areas based on their core competencies and commercial experience. 4.1 Pillar 1: Market Position & Differentiation Question 1.1 (Core Competencies): Outline your primary services and expertise, such as previous projects in a similar scope, or any COTS options you currently off

description: Настоящата поръчка предвижда да се доставят чрез закупуване нови, неупотребявани маслонапълнени разпределителни трансформатори с регулиране на напрежението под товар за нуждите на „Електроразпределение Север” АД. 1. Доставка на Трансформатор, маслен, херметичен 250/21 с автоматично регулиране - 70 броя. 2. Доставка на Трансформатор, маслен, херметичен 400/21 с автоматично регулиране - 30 броя. title: Bulgaria – Telescopic sights – „Доставка на оптически прибори, чрез сключване на рамкови споразумения по три самостоятелно обособени позиции“.
description: Предметът на обществената поръчка е „Доставка на оптически прибори, чрез сключване на рамкови споразумения по три самостоятелно обособени позиции“, както следва: Обособена позиция № 1 „Доставка на монокуляр за нощно виждане ”, съгласно ТС О 33.4578.24 – ВО; Обособена позиция № 2 „Доставка на нощен оптически мерник за стрелково оръжие“, съгласно ТС О 33.4579.24 – ВО; Обособена позиция № 3 „Доставка на дневен оптически мерник“, съгласно ТС О 33.4927.25 – ВО. Обществената поръчка не съдържа класифицирана информация по смисъла на § 2, т. 20 от Допълнителните разпоредби на ЗОП. Рамковите споразумения за всяка обособена позиция ще бъдат сключени с едно лице – участникът, класиран на първо място и определен за изпълнител по съответната обособена позиция. В Рамковите споразумения са определени всички условия и на основание чл. 82, ал. 1 от ЗОП, Възложителят ще сключва конкретни договори, като прилага тези условия. - По Обособена позиция № 1 „Доставка на монокуляр за нощно виждане ”, съгласно ТС О 33.4578.24 – ВО - общото прогнозно количество, което се предвижда да бъде доставено до 2960 броя, разпределена (прогнозно) по години за целия срок на действие на рамковото споразумение. - По Обособена позиция № 2 „Доставка на нощен оптически мерник за стрелково оръжие“, съгласно ТС О 33.4579.24 – ВО - общото прогнозно количество, което се предвижда да бъде доставено до 1228 броя, разпределена (прогнозно) по години за целия срок на действие на рамковото споразумение. - По Обособена позиция № 3 „Доставка на дневен оптически мерник“, съгласно ТС О 33.4927.25 – ВО - общото прогнозно количество, което се предвижда да бъде доставено е до 1439 броя, разпределена (прогнозно) по години за целия срок на действие на рамковото споразумение.

description: Η παρούσα μελέτη αφορά την μίσθωση μηχανημάτων και φορτηγών, με την μορφή έξι (6) ομάδων, ως εξής: 1η ομάδα αποτελούμενη από έναν (1) ερπυστριοφόρο υδραυλικό εκσκαφέα (>120 ΗΡ) και ένα (1) φορτηγό ανατρεπόμενο, 2η ομάδα αποτελούμενη από έναν (1) ερπυστριοφόρο υδραυλικό εκσκαφέα (>120 ΗΡ) και ένα (1) φορτηγό ανατρεπόμενο, 3η ομάδα αποτελούμενη από έναν (1) ερπυστριοφόρο υδραυλικό εκσκαφέα (>50 ΗΡ έως 120 HP) και ένα (1) φορτηγό ανατρεπόμενο, 4η ομάδα αποτελούμενη από δύο (2) ερπυστριοφόρους υδραυλικούς εκσκαφείς (>120 ΗΡ) και δύο (2) φορτηγά ανατρεπόμενα, 5η ομάδα αποτελούμενη από δύο (2) ερπυστριοφόρους υδραυλικούς εκσκαφείς (>120 ΗΡ) και δύο (2) φορτηγά ανατρεπόμενα, 6η ομάδα αποτελούμενη από δύο (2) ερπυστριοφόρους υδραυλικούς εκσκαφείς (>120 ΗΡ) και δύο (2) φορτηγά ανατρεπόμενα. Συγκεκριμένα τα μισθωμένα μηχανήματα με τη μορφή ομάδων – συνεργείων, θα χρησιμοποιηθούν για τον καθαρισμό κοίτης και συγκεκριμένα την απομάκρυνση απορριμμάτων και μπαζών, για απομάκρυνση βλάστησης (καλαμιών, θάμνων, δέντρων), για άρση λοιπών εμποδίων (ξεροί κορμοί, κ.λπ.), για διαμόρφωση πρανών για την αποφυγή καταπτώσεων, για φόρτωση και μεταφορά προϊόντων καθαρισμού σε κατάλληλους χώρους καθώς και για τοπικές αποκαταστάσεις ζημιών σε αναχώματα. Οι ως άνω περιγραφόμενες εργασίες θα πραγματοποιηθούν με απώτερο σκοπό την ελεύθερη απορροή των υδάτων σε ρέματα, υδατορέματα, χειμάρρους και ποταμούς στα γεωγραφικά όρια της Περιφερειακής Ενότητας Ροδόπης, τα οποία θα υποδειχτούν από την Υπηρεσία μας και είναι συγκεκριμένα τα παρακάτω δεκαέξι (16) σημεία επέμβασης: Ρέμα Δυτικά Οικισμού Αμαξάδων, Ρέμα Ανατολικά Οικισμού Αμαξάδων ή Αμυγδαλόρεμα, Ρέμα Ασκητών, Ρέμα Βοσβόζη ή Ασπρόρεμα, Ρέμα Γλυφάδας 1, Ρέμα Γλυφάδας 2, Ρέμα Καλλυντηρίου, Ρέμα Μαυρομματίου 1, Ρέμα Μαυρομματίου 2, Ρέμα Παγουρίων, Ρέμα Πανεπιστημιούπολης, Ρέμα Παραδημής ή Χηνόρεμα, Ρέμα Πελαγίας, Ρέμα Πλατανίτη, Ρέμα Πλησίον Ηφαίστου, Ρέμα Φαναρίου. Οι ώρες εργασίας (διάρκεια μίσθωσης) της κάθε ομάδας είναι: ΟΜΑΔΑ ΩΡΕΣ ΜΙΣΘΩΣΗΣ 1η ΟΜΑΔΑ 1000 2η ΟΜΑΔΑ 1000 3η ΟΜΑΔΑ 1581,7672 4η ΟΜΑΔΑ 1000 5η ΟΜΑΔΑ 1300 6η ΟΜΑΔΑ 2000 Οι ώρες εργασίας του κάθε συνεργείου, υπολογίζονται ότι θα εξαντληθούν συνεχόμενα ή τμηματικά, σε χρονική διάρκεια είκοσι τεσσάρων (24) μηνών, όπως αναλυτικότερα περιγράφεται στη Τεχνική Περιγραφή και Προϋπολογισμό της παροχής υπηρεσίας, προϋπολογισμού 2.000.000,00 € συμπεριλαμβανομένου Φ.Π.Α.

title: Automated Celestial Navigation System (ACNS) Production
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS PUBLISHED FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THE GOVERNMENT IS NOT SEEKING OR ACCEPTING UNSOLICITED PROPOSALS. This notice is a Request for Information (RFI) as defined in FAR 15.101(c). The Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) is conducting market research for the Automated Celestial Navigation System (ACNS). ACNS helps to determine vessel position based on optical sighting of celestial objects including stars and resident space objects (RSOs) such as satellites and space debris. Ship�s position derived from ACNS shall be used to improve the resilience of the surface ship Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) system of systems suite by providing an Alternative Position Source (APS) to support Assured PNT. U.S. Navy and commercial enterprises leverage a variety of navigation solutions that allow vessels to safely navigate with and without GPS. The U.S. Navy is looking to modernize legacy systems over time. This RFI seeks information on prospective technologies that could be leveraged or developed as enablers for an ACNS solution. This RFI seeks to understand how interested parties would integrate the ACNS with navigation sensors and other ship equipment specifically Global Positioning System-Based Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Service (GPNTS). PAE MS invites all interested potential sources, including small business concerns, to submit written information sufficient to demonstrate the respondent�s ability to fulfill the requirements. For those interested parties that have technologies which may not achieve a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 8-9 by FY 2029, please provide information on current research and development efforts that may address some or all requirements of this RFI beyond FY 2029. Responses are requested by 27 November 2026. Questions or clarifications related to this RFI may be submitted electronically to Ms. Liz Bonilla-Sotomayor at liz.c.bonilla-sotomayor.civ@us.navy.mil and Ms. Andrea Longo at andrea.t.longo.civ@us.navy.mil. Verbal questions will not be accepted. Questions shall not contain classified information. Please ensure that the subject line of any emails containing responses or questions related to this notice includes the name of your firm and �Automated Celestial Navigation System (ACNS) RFI Response� (without quotation marks) in the subject line. Responses are limited to a maximum of fifteen (15) pages in length, excluding the cover page, within a minimum font size of 10 points. Generic capability statements that do not address the information requested in this RFI will be deemed non-responsive without any further communication from the Government. All responsive submissions received by the due date noted in this RFI may be considered by the Government to inform the resulting Request for Proposal. All information received bearing proprietary markings will be handled in accordance with applicable statutes and regulations. Responses to this notice will not be returned and will be maintained or destroyed in accordance with the Government�s records management policy. An acknowledgement of receipt will be provided for all responses received. If you do not receive an acknowledgement within two working days, please notify the points of contact listed in this notice. All materials submitted in response to this RFI should be UNCLASSIFIED. Responses to this notice must include the following: Include a cover page containing the following information: Sources Sought number for this notice (N00024-27-IWS-6-0002) Company Name Mailing address and physical address (if different) DUNS number CAGE code Business size status (based on NAICS code 334511) Type of small business (if applicable) Facility Security Clearance (FSC) level Name, position, email address, and phone number of point(s) of contact Interested parties submitting proposed solutions shall include the following in the RFI submission: Provide System Characteristics: Average position fix accuracy of the proposed system; Operational capabilities across day, twilight, and nighttime conditions; Ephemeris data age for fix accuracy; How quality of each position fix is indicated; Ability of the system to accept data formats sourced from the United States Naval Observatory (USNO); Type of Earth Orientation Parameter (EOP) data format; Average position fix frequency rate (for Stars-Only and Stars-Satellites). Provide Component Characteristics: 1) What is the current configuration of the proposed system? 2) Sensor volume and physical dimensions; 3) Sensor weight; 4) What environmental Military Standards does your proposed system meet (i.e. MIL-STD-810H CH1 (Environmental Engineering Considerations and Laboratory Tests), MIL-STD-167-1A (Mechanical Vibrations of Shipboard Equipment), MIL-DTL-901E (High-Impact Mechanical Shock for Shipboard Machinery and Equipment), and MIL-STD-461H (Electromagnetic Interference Characteristics of Subsystems and Equipment)? Additional Information: Anticipated development timeline if not currently in production; How the solution will be phased over time; Additional technologies that can be leveraged to support a robust ACNS solution; Sensors supported (e.g. radars, Electro-Optical/Infrared (EO/IR), Automatic Identification System (AIS), etc.); Interfaces supported (including physical and digital integration with GPNTS); Projected cost drivers or potential major cost drivers; Projected schedule drivers or potential major schedule drivers; Identification of relevant technology risk areas and any ongoing technology maturation initiatives currently under way; Information concerning your ability at conducting and supporting the full-range of current Model Based Systems Engineering � Digital Engineering (MBSE-DE) features to consider in a Contractor-Government partnership with a vision for balancing benefits of digital engineering collaboration against additional upfront and long-term costs and learning curves; The ability to build ACNS based on a government-provided Level III Technical Data Packages (TDPs) and other design specific documentation, if provided. Please identify any proprietary technology or information integral to your proposed solution that could potentially limit future Government production or sustainment efforts. Comment on your company�s willingness to provide Government Purpose Rights for any identified proprietary technology or information. Identify any obstacles to competition in the areas of production, engineering support, or defined scope of work that would hinder or restrict your company�s involvement in a competitive future procurement. In addition, recommend solutions or mitigation paths for the Navy to overcome the obstacles. This notice is not a request for proposals. Per FAR 15.101(c), responses to this notice do not constitute offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation or obligation on the part of the Government. All information contained in this notice is preliminary in nature and is subject to change. The Government makes no representations that a solicitation for the requirements described in this notice will be issued. Respondents are wholly responsible for any costs or expenses associated with submitting a response. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this notice or any further requests for information relating to a response. Respondents will not be notified of the results of this notice. The information obtained from submitted responses may be used by the Government in the development of a procurement strategy. title: Light Interference Filter (LIF)
description: DLA Weapons Support at Aberdeen is issuing solicitation SPRBL127RA008 as a competitive Request for Proposal (RFP) on October 28, 2026, for a five (5) year, Firm-Fixed Price (FFP), Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (ID/IQ) type contract, with a proposed maximum contract value of $8,677,861.69. The proposed action is for the acquisition of Light Interference Filter (LIF), NSN: 5855-01-379-1410. The Government owns the Technical Data Package (TDP), which is the Light Interference Filter Performance Specification, for this item. The solicitation will include instructions to request these documents. Due to the sensitive nature of this item, potential sources will have to request and receive authorization prior to the release of this information. Night Vision Devices and components, and their associated technical data, are restricted from export by the International Trafficking in Arms Regulation (ITAR), Part 121, Category XII. The TDP is subject to the Internal Traffic in Arms Regulations. Any Offeror who wants to request a copy of the TDP must be registered in the Joint Certification Program, website is below: https://public.logisticsinformationservice.dla.mil/PublicHome/jcp/default.aspx Requests for a copy of the TDP after the RFP is issued must include proof of DD Form 2345 JCP Certification and proof of Facility Security Clearance (FCL) / Level of Safeguarding for Classified Information / Material of SECRET / SECRET. The documents to retrieve the TDP are attached to this solicitation. First Article Testing (FAT) will be required, which will be detailed in the solicitation. An Offeror may request a FAT waiver if certain conditions are met. A DD Form 254 Contract Security Classification Specification is part of this requirement and will be included in the RFP. To be eligible for award, an Offeror will be required to have access to classified data. The required Facility Security Clearance (FCL) / Level of Safeguarding for Classified Information / Material is SECRET / SECRET. The anticipated hardware ship to location will be W25G1U, New Cumberland, PA. The Government required delivery will be listed in the solicitation. Please do not wait until the last minute to submit your proposals once the solicitation is issued. To avoid potential submission of a late proposal, we recommend the transmission of your proposal file 24 hours prior to the required proposal due date and time. Place of Contract Performance: 6565 Surveillance Loop, Room C1-301 Aberdeen Proving Ground, MD 21005-1846 Point of Contact(s): Amber Owens / Amber.Owens@dla.mil / 443-243-2236 Rus Shah / Rusabh.Shah@dla.mil / 443-883-1075

title: Schellenbergweg - Schellenbergstrasse, Masanserstrasse bis Giacomettistrasse, Baumeisterarbeiten
description:
. Die IBC Energie Wasser Chur befindet sich in der schrittweisen Realisierung ihres Wärmenetzes. In einer weiteren Etappe erfolgt nun der Bau der Wärmeleitungen, welche für die Versorgung der entsprechenden Gebäude entlang vom Schellenbergweg und der Schellenbergstrasse vorgesehen sind.

title: BKP 421 Gärtnerarbeit
description:
Das Schulhaus Zelg in Kirchdorf befindet sich am Dorfrand, direkt angrenzend an das Naherholungs- und Naturschutzgebiet des Gerzensees. Die Schulanlage besteht aus dem Schulhaus (1976), Turnhalle (1989) und Kindergartenanbau (2015). Der Aussenbereich dient als Pausenraum sowie Sport- und Spielplatz.


Das Projekt umfasst die Sanierung des Schulhauses und der Turnhalle sowie einen Anbau an das bestehende Schulhaus. Am Kindergartenanbau werden keine Massnahmen getroffen. Die Bauphasen werden etappiert umgesetzt und in Teilbereiche Anbau, Schulhaus, Turnhalle und Umgebung gegliedert.

title: Sanierung Stationsstrasse/Kreuzwiesenstrasse, Baumeister- und Belagsarbeiten
description:
. Die Gemeinde Landquart saniert, ersetzt und erneuert in der Stationsstrasse sowie der Kreuzwiesenstrasse ihre bestehenden Werkleitungen.

. Neben dem Ersatz der Wasserleitungen sowie einem Teil der Mischabwasserleitungen erfolgt auch der Neubau der Meteorabwasserleitungen (Trennsystem).

. Zudem ergänzt und erweitert die Repower ihr elektrisches Kabeltrassee im Bereich der besagten Strassen.

. Weiter erfolgt der Umbau der bestehenden Haltestellen Gruobhof und Luxgasse gemäss dem Behindertengleichstellungsgesetz (BehiG).

title: Sanierung Giacomettistrasse, Aspermontstrasse - Wiesentalstrasse / Rohrbauer
description:
. An der Giacomettistrasse, auf dem Abschnitt Aspermontstrasse - Wiesentalstrasse erfolgt eine Sanierung der Werkleitungen sowie teilweise des Strassenoberbaus und der Beläge. Es werden die Werkleitungen Abwasser (teilweise), Wasser, Gas (teilweise neu, mehrheitlich Rückbau) und Strom erneuert sowie die Wärmeleitungen neu erstellt. Sämtliche Randabschlüsse werden erneuert. Der Grünstreifen sowie das angrenzende Trottoir bleiben bestehen. Die Fahrbahn beträgt neu 6.00m. Das Trottoir auf der Seite Aspermontstrasse wird mit einem Grünstreifen und Parkplätzen angepasst.

An der Wiesentalstrasse auf dem Abschnitt Haus 135 bis 143 erfolgt ein Ersatz der Wasserleitung, der Rückbau der Gasleitung sowie der Neubau der Wärmeleitungen inkl. Hausanschlüssen. Auf diesem Abschnitt erfolgt zudem der Ersatz der Asphaltbeläge in der Fahrbahn sowie ein Teilersatz der Randabschlüsse.


. Die IBC Energie Wasser Chur befindet sich in der schrittweisen Ausbauphase ihrer Wärmenetze. In einer weiteren Etappe erfolgt nun auf den oben beschriebenen Abschnitten der Bau der entsprechenden Hauptleitungen sowie der jeweiligen Hausanschlussleitungen für die Wärmeversorgung.

. Dabei handelt es sich um die folgenden Wärmeleitungen.

- Wärmeleitungen, DN 200 (da 219,1/Da 400m)

- Wärmeleitungen, DN 150 (da 168,3/Da 315mm)

- Wärmeleitungen, DN 80 (da 88,9/Da 200mm)

- Wärmeleitungen, DN 40 (da 48,3/Da 140mm)

title: Strategisk evaluering af Aalborg Kommunes deltagelse i byudviklingsselskabet Stigsborg P/S og udviklingen af Stigsborg Havnefront
description: Aalborg Kommune ønsker en uvildig evaluering af kommunens deltagelse i byudviklingsselskabet Stigsborg P/S. Evalueringen skal belyse de økonomiske, organisatoriske, juridiske og markedsmæssige konsekvenser af den valgte udviklingsmodel samt identificere de erfaringer og læringspunkter, der kan understøtte Aalborg Kommunes planlægning og gennemførelse af de kommende etaper af Stigsborg Havnefront. title: Spain – Hotel accommodation services – concesión del servicio de explotación del Hotel Oromana (C-2026/032)
description: El objeto del presente contrato es la concesión del servicio de explotación del Hotel Oromana, de titularidad municipal, situado en el municipio de Alcalá de Guadaíra, que comprende la gestión integral del establecimiento, así como la ejecución de las actuaciones necesarias de rehabilitación, reforma, posible ampliación y adecuación del inmueble para su correcto funcionamiento y mejora de categoría, todo ello conforme a lo establecido en el correspondiente pliego de prescripciones técnicas. La presente contratación tiene como finalidad la transformación integral del establecimiento hotelero, con el objetivo de su adecuación a los estándares actuales del sector y su posicionamiento como hotel de cuatro estrellas, mediante la ejecución de las actuaciones constructivas necesarias y la implantación de un modelo de gestión profesionalizado, eficiente y orientado a la calidad. No se pretende con esta licitación una mera explotación del establecimiento en su estado actual, sino la definición y desarrollo de un proyecto global y coherente que integre la intervención sobre el inmueble con un modelo de gestión hotelera alineado con el valor patrimonial, paisajístico y turístico del entorno en el que se inserta, contribuyendo a reforzar la identidad y singularidad del destino. En este sentido, la concesión deberá orientarse a la creación de una oferta hotelera de calidad, capaz de atraer tanto a visitantes como a usuarios locales, generando actividad económica, empleo y sinergias con otros sectores vinculados al turismo, la cultura y la hostelería, y actuando como elemento dinamizador del municipio y su entorno. Asimismo, el contrato comprende tanto la ejecución de las obras definidas como obligatorias, como, en su caso, la incorporación de mejoras propuestas por los licitadores, así como la gestión integral del establecimiento, incluyendo todos los servicios necesarios para su correcto funcionamiento. El detalle y alcance de todas estas prestaciones se desarrollan en el pliego de prescripciones técnicas que rige la presente contratación.
